title: A linear shape trend raises held-year error in eight main Kepler Q1 to Q16 tests of KIC 3749404
abstract: We test a simple measure of light-curve shape change in the known heartbeat binary KIC 3749404. We fit 30 orbital harmonics and a linear baseline in each of 16 Kepler release 25 quarters. We remove a brightness scale and a phase shift from harmonics 2 to 10. A time trend with four detector-season terms raises held-year squared error in all four years for aperture flux and all four years for corrected flux. Error ratios are 1.038 to 1.393 and 1.028 to 1.209. A sampled synthetic tide with a 2-degree-per-year change gives ratios below 0.114. The test can recover this simple injected shape change but does not give useful prediction in the real data under the main fit. Quadratic baselines change one of four aperture-flux error ratios to 0.975. This result limits this method. It does not reject the published apsidal-motion model, find a new object, or identify an instrument cause. Both flux products use the same exposures. Independent observations are absent. Code, accepted samples, input hashes, controls, and offline instructions are included.

display.caption: Quarter shape scores after gain and phase removal, fitted three-year change, and held-year prediction error. The score direction uses all quarters and is descriptive. The held-year fits use training data only. Ratios above one show worse prediction with a time trend.
